RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 20

The panel's gender composition alone is not evidence of bias or discrimination. Committees frequently comprise a single gender due to staffing availability and existing leadership demographics.

Once candidates reach the final interview stage, paper qualifications matter less than interview performance, references, strategic vision, and institutional fit. While you hold stronger administrative qualifications, the panel may have valued her ten years of classroom experience or her performance across the two interviews.

Raising gender without tangible evidence—such as discriminatory remarks or procedural breaches—is legally unsubstantiated and could seriously harm your professional standing. Instead, send a polite follow-up requesting your written feedback to understand how the decision was reached.
